text:
Tom sails from 1 PM to 4 PM, which is a duration of 3 hours.  
At a speed of 10 miles per hour, the distance traveled is:  
\[ \text{Distance} = 10 \text{ mph} \times 3 \text{ hours} = 30 \text{ miles} \]  

On the return trip, he travels at 6 miles per hour. The time required to cover 30 miles is:  
\[ \text{Time} = \frac{30 \text{ miles}}{6 \text{ mph}} = 5 \text{ hours} \]  

Answer: 5 hours
reasoning:
We are given: "Tom's ship can travel at 10 miles per hour. He is sailing from 1 to 4 PM. He then travels back at a rate of 6 mph. How long does it take him to get back?"

Interpretation: Tom sails from a starting point to a destination from 1 PM to 4 PM at 10 mph. The time from 1 PM to 4 PM is 3 hours. Distance = speed * time = 10 mph * 3 hours = 30 miles.

Then he travels back at 6 mph. Time to get back = distance / speed = 30 miles / 6 mph = 5 hours.

The question asks: "How long does it take him to get back?" So the answer is 5 hours.
